text_blocks.snippet: Freedom Mortgage's interest rates vary based on loan type, term, and individual borrower qualifications. For example, a 30-year conventional mortgage may have an average interest rate of 6.90%, while a 30-year FHA loan might be around 6.34% according to The Mortgage Reports. A 30-year VA loan could have a rate of 6.14%, and a 15-year conventional loan might be 6.19%. Interest rates are also affected by other factors like credit score and down payment.

list.title: Conventional Loans:
list.snippet: 30-year fixed-rate mortgages have an average rate around 6.90%, while 15-year mortgages are typically lower.

list.title: FHA Loans:
list.snippet: 30-year FHA loans are often lower than conventional loans, with an average rate around 6.34%.

list.title: VA Loans:
list.snippet: 30-year VA loans tend to have competitive rates, often lower than conventional and FHA loans for the same term.

list.title: Adjustable-Rate Mortgages (ARMs):
list.snippet: ARMs have an introductory fixed-rate period, followed by interest rate adjustments, which can be higher or lower than the initial rate depending on market conditions.
Credit Score: A higher credit score generally results in a lower interest rate.
Down Payment: A larger down payment can lead to a lower interest rate.
Loan Type: Different loan types (conventional, FHA, VA) have different average rates.
Loan Term: Shorter loan terms (e.g., 15-year) usually have lower interest rates than longer terms (e.g., 30-year).
Market Conditions: Interest rates fluctuate based on overall economic conditions and the Federal Reserve's policies.
